title: Salesloft Drift OAuth token abuse against Salesforce tenants
confirmed_facts: Google Cloud reported that UNC6395 used compromised OAuth tokens associated with Salesloft Drift for discovery and bulk exfiltration from Salesforce tenants.
Google Cloud characterized the activity as high-volume API access and silent bulk customer-data export.
inferences: Connected SaaS applications require explicit vendor-compromise blast-radius and export controls beyond OAuth callback correctness.
trust_boundaries: customer tenant to connected SaaS app
SaaS token holder to bulk customer data
control_hypotheses: Token inventory and revocation must be tenant-aware and measurable for every connected app.
Bulk export controls need volume, velocity, field, tenant, and anomaly boundaries independent of a provider's nominal OAuth scope.
A vendor-compromise exercise should test rapid grant revocation and residual cached access.

regression.mutation: Add a tenant-wide refresh token and unbounded bulk export with no inventory owner, rate ceiling, or revocation test.
